text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

In the AFL, Brisbane co-captain and Brownlow Medallist Michael Voss, who is crucial to Brisbane in the lead up to the finals, may miss the rest of the season after sustaining a suspected strained posterior cruciate ligament in the right knee in the match agains St Kilda at Waverley Park. Page 27.

North Sydney rugby league president Ray Beattie, Norths football club executive Bob Saunders, and Norths Leagues Club chief executive Jim Henry will make a critical presentation to the Central Coast Leagues Club tonight concerning plans for Norths to relocate to Gosford. Page 32.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Several members of the Australian contingent preparing to compete at the world athletics championships in Athens have withdrawn because of injury. High jumper Tim Forsyth withdrew after aggravating an injury, triple jumper Andrew Murphy is out with a back injury, and seven more athletes did not compete at the meeting in Hungary designed to provide their last test of form. Page 25.

New Zealand All Blacks rugby union coach John Hart says the Australian Wallabies should bring five-eighth David Knox back into the team and stop chopping and changing the team's line up. Hart's comments came after his team beat Australia 33-18 in the Bledisloe Cup Test match in Melbourne on Saturday night. Page 29.

Manly rugby league coach Bob Fulton has been criticised by Australian Rugby League referees director Michael Stone for saying referee David Manson may have been responsible for Manly's loss to Parramatta on Friday night and for suggesting video referees should be brought in for the semi-finals. Page 30.
THE AGE

Australian high jumper Tim Forsyth has withdrawn from the Australian team at the world athletics championships in Athens because of a strained medial ligament. Forsyth was Australia's best hope for a medal in the men's competition. Page 4.

The National Basketball League hosted its All-Stars weekend this weekend, which saw North defeat South 151-142 at the Sydney Entertainment Centre on Saturday night. North's Derek Rucker led the team with 28 points followed by Robert Rose with 23 and Isaac Burton with 26. Page 18.

The Melbourne Phoenix netball team has fallen from the top of the national netball league after being defeated by the Sydney Sandpipers 61-53 in Sydney this weekend. The Sandpipers' win brings them up to fourth place and allows the Adelaide Thunderbirds to take top position on the ladder. Page 20.
THE HERALD SUN

South Melbourne soccer club president George Vasilopoulos said last night the club was fighting to survive in the Ericsson Cup because of a decision by Soccer Australia to find both South and Sydney United guilty of bringing the game into disrepute following violent scenes during the two teams' preliminary final last season. Page 90.

A spiteful Australian Football League match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground yesterday between Collingwood and Melbourne has left Collingwood's Matthew Francis and Paul Williams facing video scrutiny - Francis for a possibly kneeing Melbourne's Jim Stynes in the groin, and Williams for an off-the-ball incident with Paul Hopgood. Page 94.

Following the Richmond Australian Football League club's defeat by Adelaide at Footy Park on the weekend, president Leon Daphne said the team, which is sitting at 15th position, is out of the finals hunt. Daphne said the weekend's 137-point loss was the worst defeat since he became president in 1993. Page 93.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian Super Touring motor racing champion Brad Jones was sitting in seventh position yesterday in the Spa 24-hour endurance event in Brussels. Jones' effort with teammates Yvan Muller of France and Tamara Vidali from Italy was hampered by cramps and heavy rain. Page 29.

While in preparation for the world athletics championships which begin in Athens on Saturday, Australian sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor won the 100 metre and 200 metre events at a low-key grand prix meeting in Budapest. Australian Nova Peris-Kneebone ran second in both races. Page 50.

The Hunter Mariners Super League team moved closer to winning a place in the quarter finals of the World Club Challenge after defeating Paris 32-0 at Topper Stadium in Newcastle yesterday. Within 28 minutes Hunter jumped from a 4-0 to its final 32-0 lead. Page 37.
